question: What is the primary goal of health education?

options.A: Voluntary behavioral change for better health

explanation: Health education aims to empower people to change their habits willingly through increased understanding rather than force. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T1#GNS124_U5_T1_h1)

question: Why does explaining the reason behind a health practice improve compliance?

options.A: It bridges the gap between knowledge and actual practice
options.B: It eliminates all cultural beliefs instantly
options.C: It replaces the need for community health workers entirely
options.D: It guarantees immediate funding from the government

explanation: Understanding the underlying cause helps individuals see the personal relevance of adopting a new behavior. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T1#GNS124_U5_T1_h1)

question: A key objective of health education in primary health care is promoting what?

options.A: Total dependence on foreign medical aid

explanation: Primary health care focuses on building local capacity so communities can handle basic health needs independently. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T1#GNS124_U5_T1_h2)

question: How does health education improve the utilization of primary health facilities?

options.A: By converting health posts into full surgical centers
options.B: By teaching people when and how to seek early care
options.C: By providing free transport vehicles for every household
options.D: By increasing the salary of nurses working in rural clinics

explanation: Educated communities recognize early symptoms and visit clinics promptly instead of waiting for complications. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T1#GNS124_U5_T1_h2)

question: Which principle requires involving the community actively rather than just lecturing?
explanation: Active participation ensures that learners engage with the material and take ownership of their health actions. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T1#GNS124_U5_T1_h3)

question: Why is addressing seasonal health issues an application of the principle of relevance?

options.A: It matches the current health threats facing the community
options.B: It prevents the government from buying medications
options.C: It reduces the workload of clinic nurses significantly
options.D: It guarantees financial rewards for the educators

explanation: Relevance means teaching about problems people are actively experiencing, such as malaria during the rains. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T1#GNS124_U5_T1_h3)

question: What component of the Health Belief Model refers to a person's belief in their own ability to take action?
explanation: Self-efficacy is the confidence an individual has in successfully performing a recommended health behavior. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T1#GNS124_U5_T1_h4)

question: A pregnant woman refuses to attend antenatal care because the clinic is too far and transport cost is high. Which HBM concept does this represent?
explanation: Distance and cost are tangible obstacles that hinder behavior adoption, fitting the definition of perceived barriers. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T1#GNS124_U5_T1_h4)

question: Which educational method reaches the largest number of people simultaneously?
explanation: Radio, television, and billboards fall under mass approaches designed to broadcast information to wide populations. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T1#GNS124_U5_T1_h5)

question: What is the main advantage of using a group approach over a mass approach in rural health education?

options.A: It allows participants to ask questions and discuss freely
options.B: It requires zero preparation from the community nurse
options.C: It guarantees that every single villager will attend
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for visual aids

explanation: Group sessions foster interaction, peer learning, and immediate clarification of doubts. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T1#GNS124_U5_T1_h5)

question: What is the very first step in planning a community health education program?
explanation: You must first discover what problems exist before designing educational interventions to solve them. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T1#GNS124_U5_T1_h6)

question: Why must program objectives be measurable during the planning phase?

options.A: To accurately determine if the goals were achieved during evaluation
options.B: To prevent community members from asking difficult questions
options.C: To make the written report look professional and long
options.D: To satisfy strict international funding requirements only

explanation: Measurable objectives give clear criteria to judge whether the intervention was successful. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T1#GNS124_U5_T1_h6)

question: Which factor is NOT a common barrier to health education in resource-limited settings?

options.B: Erratic electricity supply for electronic aids
options.D: Excessive availability of trained health educators

explanation: A shortage, rather than an excess, of trained health personnel is a major hurdle in community health. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T1#GNS124_U5_T1_h7)

question: What type of evaluation is conducted during the actual implementation of a program to make adjustments?
explanation: Formative evaluation happens while the program is running so educators can correct course immediately. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T1#GNS124_U5_T1_h8)

question: Why is measuring changes in health statistics more reliable than simply asking attendees if they enjoyed a lecture?

options.A: It shows actual behavioral impact rather than mere politeness
options.B: It stops people from asking questions about the disease
options.C: It takes less time than handing out evaluation questionnaires
options.D: It proves that the health workers were paid their salaries

explanation: People may praise a speaker out of courtesy, but concrete health data reveals true adoption of healthy practices. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T1#GNS124_U5_T1_h8)
